gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-permits-per-second: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-permits-per-second: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-permits-per-second: Short inference from the page's measured analogue: 'Semaphore(10), 5 ms calls: 1989 calls in one second, peak inside 10' plus 'Each permit came back when its call ended and was taken again at once. Permits bound how many calls run at once, not how many start per second' gives 10 permits x 200/s ~ 2,000, so 50 permits x 50/s ~ 2,500.
recorded.prompt:q-mutex-calls-itself: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-mutex-calls-itself: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-mutex-calls-itself: The page states 'It isn't reentrant: a thread that holds the permit and asks again waits for itself, with a plain acquire() for ever' and shows 'same thread, second tryAcquire(1, SECONDS): false'.
recorded.prompt:q-refusals-in-finally: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-refusals-in-finally: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-refusals-in-finally: Short inference: the page's refusal path (tryAcquire inside try, release in finally) shows 'Every refused caller gave back a permit it never took, raising the limit by one' with permits rising 8, 10, 11 on a Semaphore(3), so 300 refusals raise 20 to 320; that the finally also runs on a return busy() (the page's example throws) is general Java, not shown.
recorded.prompt:q-probe-on-fair-semaphore: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-probe-on-fair-semaphore: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-probe-on-fair-semaphore: The page says tryAcquire() 'takes a permit that is free at that moment, even with threads queued' on a fair semaphore and shows 'tryAcquire() took it first in 762 of 1000 runs' with one thread queued and a permit released.

recorded.prompt:q-permits-per-second:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-permits-per-second:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-permits-per-second:b: The page says permits come back 'when its call ended and was taken again at once' and 'A rate limit needs a clock: permits that come back on a schedule, not when the call ends', so a semaphore has no once-a-second return.
recorded.prompt:q-permits-per-second:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-permits-per-second:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-permits-per-second:c: Short inference: in the page's run forty threads called through ten permits and got 'peak inside 10' and 1989 calls a second, not one call per thread, so the rate tracks permits and call time, not thread count.
recorded.prompt:q-permits-per-second:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-permits-per-second:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-permits-per-second:d: Short inference: the page says 'release() puts one back and wakes a waiting thread' and the permit 'was taken again at once', with 1989 calls/s from 40 threads, so there is no per-thread release cycle capping the rate at the thread count.
recorded.prompt:q-mutex-calls-itself:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-mutex-calls-itself:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-mutex-calls-itself:b: The page shows 'one.release() from another thread: permits = 1' and says 'any thread may give a permit back, whether or not it took one', so the reason given (only another thread may release) is wrong; the thread waits for itself.
recorded.prompt:q-mutex-calls-itself:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-mutex-calls-itself:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-mutex-calls-itself:c: The page says 'So Semaphore(1) is not a lock. It isn't reentrant' and the same-thread second tryAcquire printed false.
recorded.prompt:q-mutex-calls-itself:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-mutex-calls-itself:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-mutex-calls-itself:d: The page shows the same thread's second tryAcquire returning false and says it 'waits for itself', so no permit is handed to the nested acquire.
recorded.prompt:q-refusals-in-finally:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-refusals-in-finally:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-refusals-in-finally:b: The page says 'Every refused caller gave back a permit it never took' and its summary names 'a release on a path that never acquired (a refusal ...)' as raising the limit; the return-vs-throw step is general Java.
recorded.prompt:q-refusals-in-finally:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-refusals-in-finally:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-refusals-in-finally:c: The reference table says release() 'adds 1 or n permits; no check of who calls it', and the page shows 'one.release() from another thread: permits = 1'.
recorded.prompt:q-refusals-in-finally:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-refusals-in-finally:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-refusals-in-finally:d: The wave outputs show the extra permits persisting across waves ('permits afterwards 8', then 10, then 11), and 'A pool of two now has three permits', so extra permits are not dropped after use.
recorded.prompt:q-probe-on-fair-semaphore:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-probe-on-fair-semaphore:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-probe-on-fair-semaphore:b: The page gives the real reason, 'new Semaphore(n, true) hands permits to waiting threads in arrival order. tryAcquire() ignores that order', which contradicts a creation-time cutoff only implicitly; the page never addresses the creation-time claim itself.
recorded.prompt:q-probe-on-fair-semaphore:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-probe-on-fair-semaphore:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-probe-on-fair-semaphore:c: The page attributes queue-respecting refusal to the timed form ('tryAcquire(0, TimeUnit.SECONDS) refuses when another thread is queued ahead of it'), while untimed tryAcquire() took the permit in 762 of 1000 runs.
recorded.prompt:q-probe-on-fair-semaphore:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-probe-on-fair-semaphore:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-probe-on-fair-semaphore:d: The page says release() 'puts one back and wakes a waiting thread', and the 762-of-1000 result shows a tryAcquire() after the release taking the permit before the queued thread.
